content: An acinus is the berry-shaped terminal structure of an exocrine gland where secretions are produced. Acini are present in various organs, including the stomach, the sebaceous glands of the scalp, the salivary glands of the tongue, the liver, the lacrimal glands, and the pancreas. Mucous acini typically appear pale when stained, whereas serous acini generally stain dark. Some sources use the term acinus interchangeably with alveolus, though this equivalence is not universally accepted.
